root_cause.text: NFS LOCALIO's page cache allocations used the default GFP flags (which include __GFP_FS), allowing direct memory reclaim to re-enter NFS filesystem code via nfs_writepages, causing recursion deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "susceptible to recursion deadlock via direct reclaim, e.g.: NFS LOCALIO down to XFS and then back into NFS via nfs_writepages." The patch explicitly clears __GFP_FS from the mapping's GFP mask to "prevent direct reclaim recursion back into NFS via nfs_writepages."

Calling vfs_fsync_range can initiate page writeback via nfs_writepages; if page cache allocations in the NFS LOCALIO code used default GFP flags, direct memory reclaim during this call can cause recursion deadlock.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
nfs: add LOCALIO support

Add client support for bypassing NFS for localhost reads, writes, and
commits. This is only us
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 70ba381e1a431245c137ed597ec6a05991c79bd9
Author: Weston Andros Adamson <dros@primarydata.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 5 15:09:53 2024 -0400

    nfs: add LOCALIO support
    
    Add client support for bypassing NFS for localhost reads, writes, and
    commits. This is only useful when the client and the server are
    running on the same host.
    
    nfs_local_probe() is stubbed out, later commits will enable client and
    server handshake via a Linux-only LOCALIO auxiliary RPC protocol.
bic_trace_step.reason: The code shows allocations in nfs_do_local_read (line ~340: iocb = nfs_local_iocb_alloc(hdr, localio, GFP_KERNEL);), nfs_do_local_write (line ~410: iocb = nfs_local_iocb_alloc(hdr, localio, GFP_NOIO);), and nfs_local_commit (line ~560: ctx = nfs_local_fsync_ctx_alloc(data, localio, GFP_KERNEL);). Both GFP_KERNEL and GFP_NOIO include __GFP_FS, which allows direct memory reclaim to re-enter NFS filesystem code (e.g., nfs_writepages), causing a recursion deadlock as described in the root cause. No use of GFP_NOFS or other safe flags is present, so the fix is absent.
